s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute bilateral visual disturbance with transient visual obscurations and associated auditory symptoms
salient_findings: Disc hemorrhages and exudates in the right eye
Multiple cysts in the posterior fossa
key_facts: 3-month history of bilateral blurry vision
1-month history of tinnitus
Bilateral optic disc edema
Worse optic disc edema in the right eye
Disc hemorrhages and exudates in the right eye
Less severe optic disc edema in the left eye
Multiple cysts in the posterior fossa
Large cyst at the level of the fourth ventricle
Obstructive hydrocephalus
Normal CSF analysis

shortlist.label: Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral optic disc edema and transient visual obscurations are consistent with this condition

shortlist.label: Pseudotumor Cerebri
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to idiopathic intracranial hypertension, this condition is also characterized by increased intracranial pressure without a mass lesion

shortlist.label: Posterior Fossa Arachnoid Cyst
shortlist.why_kept: The presence of a large cyst at the level of the fourth ventricle and obstructive hydrocephalus supports this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Dandy-Walker Malformation
shortlist.why_kept: The combination of bilateral optic disc edema, hydrocephalus, and a cyst in the posterior fossa makes this a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Chiari Malformation
shortlist.why_kept: The presence of a cyst in the posterior fossa and hydrocephalus, along with symptoms such as tinnitus, make this a possible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The presence of multiple cysts in the posterior fossa, including a large cyst at the level of the fourth ventricle, inducing obstructive hydrocephalus, best explains the patient's symptoms and findings, including bilateral optic disc edema and tinnitus.

rejected.label: Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension
rejected.why: Normal CSF analysis and presence of posterior fossa cysts do not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Pseudotumor Cerebri
rejected.why: Similar to Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension, normal CSF analysis and presence of posterior fossa cysts do not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Dandy-Walker Malformation
rejected.why: Typically presents in infancy or early childhood, and the described imaging findings do not match the characteristic features of Dandy-Walker Malformation

rejected.label: Chiari Malformation
rejected.why: While it can cause obstructive hydrocephalus, the primary finding of a large posterior fossa arachnoid cyst better explains the patient's presentation
